step_goal: Keep GlobalValues.json as a complete runtime-baseline profile while allowing a limited set of explainable pre-run deck-posture overlays that are documented, source-backed, and reversible.
required_inputs: Exact deck identity: deck name, deck code, resolved CardIDs, and any linked hero-power or generated-entity CardIDs that affect deck posture.
Official VisionAI source pages for JSON syntax, GlobalValues.json, and card behavior, including the documented board-value formula and documented BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus surface.
A live or bundled default GlobalValues.json baseline copied in values-block form, with baseline source path or hash recorded.
A source-backed gameplan or research contract that states pressure posture, hero-power posture, and any requested GlobalValues overlays with per-key reasons in English.
A per-key authority model that separates pre_run_overlay_allowed, copy_baseline_only, and runtime_evidence_required keys before compilation starts.
produced_outputs: reports/global_values_key_profile_report.json with one decision for every copied baseline key and every generated known overlay key.
reports/globalvalue_intent.json or equivalent contract rows for pressure bias, overlay reasons, expected effect, and rollback posture.
validation_report.json or package-validation output proving baseline completeness, values-array shape, and GameCardId correctness.
A machine-readable blocked-or-suppressed list for requested GlobalValues numeric changes that are not authorized pre-run.
documented_capabilities: Official HearthRanger docs explicitly recommend copying GlobalValues.json from the default directory and editing that copy, not inventing a fresh partial file.
Official docs define board value as own hand, hero, hero power, weapon, secret, minions, and deck minus the corresponding opponent components.
Official docs define Final board value = first turn board value * FirstTurnValueWeight + second turn board value * SecondTurnValueWeight, with default 0 and 1 weights and an aggro example of 1 and 0.
Official card-behavior docs expose BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus as a documented runtime surface, so hero-power posture can be expressed more locally than with deck-wide tuning alone.
Official docs show GlobalValues rows as values arrays with string values and conditions, so HSConfig can preserve block shape while changing authorized numeric values.
Official docs acknowledge that many other global values exist but do not provide a complete machine-readable semantic catalog for every key.
current_hsconfig_support: HSConfig already builds GlobalValues.json baseline-first from the runtime default when available and falls back to a bundled baseline when it is not.
HSConfig already profiles every copied key, classifies keys, and emits a complete GlobalValues.json plus a key-profile report.
HSConfig already supports explainable overlay reasons per key and records changed versus unchanged keys.
HSConfig already supports pre-run turn-weight overlays driven by aggression-profile speed and can raise MyHeroPowerValue through a documented overlay path.
HSConfig already adds known overlay defaults such as MyHeroPowerValue when the runtime baseline does not contain that key, then validates the result against the baseline and profile.
observed_gap: HSConfig does not yet expose one explicit authority matrix that tells callers which GlobalValues keys are safe for static pre-run posture overlays versus which keys must stay baseline-only or runtime-evidence-only.

The current implementation can express pressure posture through overlay bundles, but broad pressure-oriented numeric changes are not yet governed by a first-class per-key authorization contract with blocked reasons.

Turn-weight overlays are currently implementation-driven, while the official docs describe a stronger aggro example; the repo needs one declared policy for when to use softer ratios versus stronger documented examples.
Hero-power posture is supported, but the contract boundary between a safe static hero-power assumption and a blocked runtime-only hero-power tuning change is not yet explicit enough.
There is no dedicated report that cleanly distinguishes requested-but-blocked broad GlobalValues tuning from authorized pre-run posture overlays.
aggressive_generation_policy: Always start from the full copied baseline and require a decision for every key; stronger generation means more explicit authority and reasoning, not fewer copied keys.

Allow FirstTurnValueWeight and SecondTurnValueWeight overlays pre-run when the gameplan contract explicitly authorizes an aggro, tempo, or pressure posture and records the expected board-value effect plus rollback to the baseline.

Allow a pre-run MyHeroPowerValue increase only when static card semantics or guide claims prove that hero-power pressure is part of the deck plan, such as a transformed damage hero power or a documented hero-power-centric archetype.
Allow small named pressure overlays only as per-key decisions with separate reason, source refs, baseline value, new value, and expected effect; never as a blanket global aggression multiplier.
Prefer card-local CARDID.json hero-power or target rows when the intent is narrow and local; reserve GlobalValues.json for deck-wide posture that the official board-value model actually covers.
Keep under-explained or weakly justified keys at copy_baseline until runtime evidence can connect them to observed board-value failures.
validation_gates: The generated GlobalValues.json must retain every baseline key, keep GameCardId equal to GlobalValues, and keep values-array block shape for every configurable key.
Every overlay must record old_value, new_value, reason, expected effect, source refs, and rollback posture before the package is considered ready.
If an overlay claims a baseline row exists, its recorded old_value must match the current copied baseline row; drift must fail closed.
Every key in the profile report must end in one of three states: baseline_confirmed, overlay_changed, or blocked_with_reason.
A requested broad multi-key pressure change must be rejected unless each affected key is separately authorized and explained.
Package validation must pass after compilation, and blocked changes must remain visible in reports instead of being silently dropped.
recommended_design_change: Add a first-class global_values_authority_matrix contract or report that assigns every GlobalValues key a category, board-value component, step1 gate, allowed pre-run overlay policy, and blocked-without-runtime-evidence policy.
Teach compile_globalvalues to consume that authority matrix so the output profile can say not only what changed, but why a requested numeric change was copied, changed, or blocked.

Split pressure posture into named pre-run overlay bundles such as turn_weight_posture, hero_power_pressure, and broad_pressure_bundle, where every bundle expands into explicit per-key rows rather than hidden heuristics.
Emit a dedicated global_values_blocked_changes.json report so guide-backed but runtime-unsafe numeric requests stay auditable instead of disappearing into generic suppression text.
Align the Step 1 contract language across HS and HSConfig so pre_run_assumption_overlay_allowed is clearly different from fresh runtime evidence authorization.
never_autogenerate_without: Never autogenerate any GlobalValues.json row without a copied baseline row or an explicit generated-overlay default that the compiler knows how to materialize safely.
Never autogenerate a broad multi-key pressure retune, a blanket increase or decrease, or a more-than-five-key pressure bundle without fresh runtime evidence and per-key authorization.

Never autogenerate opponent-global attack, health, intrinsic-value, weapon, or similar board-value component retunes from one guide sentence alone; these must remain runtime-evidence-only because they can shift many unrelated decisions.
Never autogenerate a hero-power value change when the exact transformed or deck-relevant hero-power identity is unresolved.
Never autogenerate undocumented or weakly explained GlobalValues keys simply because they appear in the baseline; baseline presence alone is enough to copy, not enough to tune.
Never autogenerate post-run style finetuning claims without baseline-hash continuity, active-config identity, legal options, outcome references, and repeated runtime evidence rows.
Never autogenerate a GlobalValues row in scalar form or any shape that diverges from the copied values-array structure.
